title: Phylogenetic Analysis of TP53 Gene in Humans for Breast Cancer Biosensors
author: Sara Da Silva Nascimento

steps.title: Acquire TP53 Gene Dataset
steps.instruction: Retrieve 301 sequences of a fragment of the human TP53 gene from GENBANK (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/popset/430765060), specifically the PopSet (430765060) provided by Hao, X.D and collaborators in 2013.

steps.title: Visualize Variable Sites
steps.instruction: Generate logos to visualize variable sites using the Weblogo3 program.

steps.title: Analyze Population Number
steps.instruction: Determine the number of populations using the Structure 2.3 program, testing both a posteriori probability and ad hoc (k) methods.

substeps.instruction: Calculate a posteriori probability using an ancestry model with mixed alleles.
Perform 20,000 interactions during the burn-in period.
Perform 200,000 Monte Carlo interactions via Markov Chain.
Increase the K value (number of populations) from 1 to 10 according to Pritchard's methodology.

steps.title: Determine Optimal Population Number
steps.instruction: Apply the Evanno method to identify the most appropriate number of populations.

substeps.instruction: Use an ad hoc amount based on the second-order rate of the likelihood function between successive K values.
Apply posteriori and k probability tests to the dataset in isolation.

steps.title: Analyze Genetic Variability
steps.instruction: Create a project in Arlequin Software 3.1 to measure molecular diversity and variance.

substeps.instruction: Calculate standard estimators: Theta (Hom, S, k, Pi).
Calculate paired and individual FST values.
Determine temporal divergence and demographic expansion indices (mismatch and Tau values) using molecular variance analysis (AMOVA).

steps.title: Test Evolutionary Molecular Signal
steps.instruction: Perform a hierarchical variance analysis using the distance matrix between all haplotype pairs.

substeps.instruction: Produce estimates of variance components analogous to Wright's F statistics using nonlinear transformations of genetic diversity estimates.
Use Mantel's Z statistic to represent divergence between possible microhabitats using the MULTIVAR (Mantel for Windows) program.
